The issued instruction is fixed 8 bytes, and is defined as follows:
--Address of slave machine, 1 byte;
--Function code, 1 byte; (only 03 function code is supported)
--Start address of reading, 2 bytes, with the high byte before and the low byte after;
--Register length of reading, 2 bytes, with the high byte before and the low byte after. The issued 
register length should be 2n, and n is a natural number, so the number of 4-byte floating-point 
numbers to be returned is n;
--CRC16 check code, 2 bytes, with the low byte before and the high byte after.
The return instruction is (5 + floating point number × 4) bytes, and is defined as follows:
--Address of slave machine, 1 byte;
--Function code, 1 byte;
--Length of returned data, 1 byte. The content is the number of floating-point numbers × 4;
--Returned data, 4n bytes. n is the number of returned data, and each data is a 4-byte single-pre-
cision floating-point number conforming to IEEE754.
--CRC16 check code, 2 bytes, with low bytes before, high bytes after.

03.  Product Overview
The SF20 series smart metal tube float flowmeter is a variable area flow meter commonly used 
in industrial automation process control. It features small size, large detection range and use 
convenience, and can be used to measure the flow of liquids, gases and steam, especially for low flow 
speed, small flow, high temperature, high pressure, strong corrosion, conductive or non-conductive 
media.
This series of metal tube float flowmeters shall conform to Q/ZKYB102.00024-2020 and JB/T 6844-
2015, and its factory acceptance test shall comply with the test procedures specified in JJG257-2007.
The product is approved by a state designated explosion-proof product quality test agency and 
meets relevant requirements of GB3836.1-2010, GB3836.2-2010 and GB3836.4-2010, and its 
explosion-proof marks are flameproof Exd IIC T1~T6Gb and intrinsically safe Exia IIC T1~T6 Gb.
4.1  Structure
04. Instrument Structure and Principle
The product is mainly composed of two parts: measuring tube and indicator. The measuring tube 
includes the conical tube or orifice plate, guide, stopper, float, etc., and the indicator includes the 
magnetic servo system, pointer, dial, circuit board (remote transmission), etc.

03
4.2  Working principle
When the measured medium flows through the measuring tube from bottom to top, the differential 
pressure is generated between the upper and lower ends of the float to form a raising force. When the 
raising force applied to the float is greater than the weight of the float immersed in fluid, the float rises, 
the area of annular space increases accordingly, the fluid flow velocity at the annular space decreases 
rapidly, and the differential pressure between the upper and lower ends of the float decreases. Finally, 
the raising force applied to the float decreases. When the raising force balances the weight of the float 
immersed in fluid, the float is stabilized at a certain position. The height of the float corresponds to the 
magnitude of the measured medium flow.
The float has built-in magnet steel, so the magnetic field changes with the movement of the float when 
the float moves up and down with the medium. The servo magnet steel fixed on the pointer shaft in 
the indicator is coupled with the magnet steel inside the float to drive the pointer and the sensing 
magnet steel to rotate. In this case, the pointer indicates the local instantaneous flow on the dial, 
which is converted into an electrical signal through the magnetic sensor, and the instantaneous flow 
and accumulated flow are displayed after processing by the circuit.

7.1  General requirements
07. Precautions for Installation and 
Operation of Instrument
The instrument is precision equipment, so it must be handled with care during transportation, 
installation, storage and operation, and rough transportation, over-stress installation and 
misplacement are prohibited. The relative position of the indicator and sensor should not be 
changed. Otherwise, it will directly affect the measurement accuracy of the instrument.
Before the installation of the instrument, the process pipeline should be swept to prevent 
the ferromagnetic substances from adhering to the pipeline, which will affect the instrument 
performance and even damage the instrument. If unavoidable, the magnetic filter should be 
installed at the instrument inlet. The instrument itself does not participate in scavenging before 
production to avoid damaging the instrument.
Before the process pipeline is installed, remove the filler stuffed against the float from the 
measuring tube (to avoid float movement during transportation), and check whether the 
instrument is damaged during transportation.
The instrument can be installed horizontally or vertically. For vertical installation, the angle 
between the center vertical line of the instrument and the plumb line should be less than 2°. For 
horizontal installation, the angle between the horizontal center line of the instrument and the 
horizontal line should be less than 2°, and the angle between the center vertical line of the vertical 
pipe and the plumb line should be less than 2°.
The nominal diameter of upstream and downstream pipes of the instrument should be the same 
as that of the instrument. The connecting flange or thread should match the flange and thread 
of the instrument. The length of the upstream straight pipe section of the instrument should be 
5 times the nominal diameter of the instrument, and the length of the downstream straight pipe 
section should be greater than or equal to 250mm.
Since the instrument transmits signals through magnetic coupling, no ferromagnetic substance 
is allowed within a radius of at least 10cm from the installation position to ensure the accuracy of 
the instrument, and the spacing should be greater than or equal to 300mm for dense side-by-side 
installation.
The instrument for measuring gas should be calibrated with air at 0.1MPa and 20°C. If the gas 
is discharged directly into the atmosphere from the instrument outlet, a pressure drop will be 
generated at the float, making the instrument pointer jitter. If this is the case, a valve should be 
installed at the instrument outlet and the valve opening should be turned down during operation.
The instrument installed in a pipe should not be subjected to stress, and the inlet and outlet of the 
instrument should be supported by a suitable pipe, so that the instrument is in the minimum stress 
state.

10
Special care should be taken during installation of the instrument lined with PTFE. Since PTFE 
deforms under pressure, an additional PTFE gasket should be installed to avoid lining flanging or 
fracturing.
During long-time use, it is inevitable that ferromagnetic substances adhere to the float in the 
pipeline. If there are too many impurities, it will jam the float or affect the measurement accuracy, 
so the measuring tube of the instrument should be cleaned regularly. If a magnetic filter is 
installed at the instrument inlet, the magnetic filter should also be cleaned regularly.
Since electronic devices are installed in the instrument indicator, during enclosure removal and 
installation or use of the instrument, tighten the screws or cover, keep the housing sealed, be sure 
to prevent liquid and ferromagnetic substances from entering, and ensure that the instrument 
enclosure is grounded reliably.
For an intelligent indicator, first ensure that the electrical wiring is correct before power on. 
Otherwise, the instrument will be easily damaged. For the operation of buttons, be sure to 
follow the operation instructions; otherwise, it will cause the data stored in the EEPROM in the 
instrument to be lost or corrupted.
The instrument should be stored in a place free of rain, snow, sunshine or corrosive gases at a 
temperature of (-40~55)°C and relative humidity not more than 90%.
During cleaning, avoid flushing the instrument housing with water to prevent water from entering 
the instrument housing, thus damaging the instrument.
As the flowmeter itself has pressure loss, the medium pressure at the installation position of the 
instrument must be greater than the flowmeter pressure loss.
For the instrument with LCD, try to avoid direct sunlight on the LCD during installation, which 
reduces the service life of the LCD.
During low temperature medium measurement, if an insulation jacket or vacuum jacket is not 
ordered, insulation treatment is required on site.
Before wiring the instrument, be sure to determine the power supply and output mode of the 
instrument, and determine the terminal numbers of power supply and signal of the circuit board 
to avoid damaging the instrument caused by wrong wiring.
The user must follow the requirements of this user's manual to ensure the correct and safe use of 
the instrument.
For the first time of use, pay attention to the following two points:
• Liquid measurement: In the process of opening the valve, to avoid damaging the instrument due to head 
impact caused by sudden opening of the valve, be sure to open the valve slowly.
• Gas measurement: Do not pressurize the pipeline before opening the valve. Otherwise, if the valve is opened 
suddenly, the float will rush to the stopper and may damage the instrument. Therefore, be sure to open the 
valve slowly. The instrument for measuring gas can be fitted with a pneumatic damping device to minimize 
float oscillation.

11
7.2  General operating requirements for explosion-proof instrument
The product enclosure should be reliably grounded during installation and use, and protected 
from the risk of ignition due to impact or friction.
The ambient temperature of the product during operation should be (-40~+60)°C.
The installation site should be free of harmful gases that have a corrosive effect on aluminum 
alloy.
Ensure that the installation site is free of combustible gases before maintenance.
The user should not replace parts of the product without authorization, and should work 
together with the product manufacturer to solve malfunctions during operation to eliminate the 
occurrence of damage.
No non-explosion-proof inspection instruments, lighting, etc. are allowed during on-site 
overhaul. Non-sparking explosion-proof tools should be used.
During installation, operation and maintenance of the instrument, comply with the relevant 
provisions of the following standards: GB3836.13-2013 Explosive atmospheres - Part 13: 
Equipment repair, overhaul and reclamation, GB/T3836.15-2017 Explosive atmospheres - Part 15: 
Electrical installations design, selection and erection, GB/T3836.16-2017 Explosive atmospheres 
- Part 16: Electrical installations inspection and maintenance and GB50257-2014 Code for 
construction and acceptance of electric equipment on fire and explosion hazard - Electrical 
equipment installation engineering.

10. Fault Analysis and Handling
10.1  Jitter 
Slight jitter: generally caused by medium fluctuation. It can be eliminated by adding a buffer 
device or lengthening the straight pipe section.
Moderate jitter: generally caused by the medium flow state. For a gas, it is generally caused by 
medium operating pressure instability. The stabilized voltage or current rectifier can be used to 
eliminate or increase the instrument gas damping.
Violent jitter: mainly caused by medium pulsation, unstable air pressure or flowmeter outlet 
having no back pressure. The voltage stabilizer, current stabilizer or buffer device can be used to 
increase the back pressure at the instrument outlet.

10.2  Pointer stopped at a certain position
10.3  Instrument pointer pointing to the maximum with the valve open
The main reason is the stuck float.
10.4  Large measurement error
The main reason is too small range of the instrument. In this case, increase the range of the 
instrument.
Generally, if the valve is opened too fast during operation of the instrument, the float impacts the 
guide upwards and fast, which deforms the guide and thus makes the float stuck. However, it is 
not ruled out that the float is stuck because the float guide rod is not concentric with the guide. 
The instrument can be removed during handling. Remove the deformed guide for shaping, and 
check whether the guide is concentric with the guide rod. If not, correct it, then refit the float, and 
push the float by hand until the float moves up and down smoothly. In addition, the instrument 
must be installed vertically or horizontally without inclination; otherwise, it is also easy to make 
the instrument stuck and cause measurement errors.
A great change in density of liquid medium is also a cause of large error. Since the medium is 
converted into the water flow in the calibration state for calibration according to the density given 
by the user before the instrument is calibrated, if the medium density changes significantly, it will 
cause a large error in the measurement. The solution is to substitute the changed medium density 
into the formula, convert it into an error correction factor, and then convert the flow measured by 
the flowmeter multiplied by the factor into the real flow.
Since the temperature and pressure have a greater effect on the gas medium, it is recommended 
to use the temperature and pressure compensation to obtain the real flow.
If the float is stuck by impurities in the measuring tube, remove the impurities.
The installation does not meet the requirements
• For vertical installation, the instrument should be kept vertical, with an inclination angle not more than 2°;
• For horizontal installation, the instrument should be kept horizontally, with an inclination angle not more 
than 2°;
• There should be no ferromagnetic substance within a radius of 100mm from the instrument;
• The installation position should be far away from the valve reducing port, pump outlet, process pipeline         
turn, etc. The lengths of the front and rear straight pipe sections should be 5D and 250mm respectively.

counterweight, rotating magnet steel and other moving parts of the instrument are loose, 
resulting in large errors. The verification can be conducted by pushing the float manually. First 
observe whether the pointer is in RP position; if so, check whether the output is 4mA and whether 
the flow is 0, and then push the float in turn to make the pointer point to the corresponding scale 
for verification. If not, adjust the position of the component. The adjustment should be made by 
professionals generally; otherwise, it will cause position loss, and the product should be returned 
to the manufacturer for correction.
For liquid measurement, if the displayed flow is greater than the actual value, the liquid viscosity 
is high in most cases and not accurately provided during ordering, and the product should be 
returned to the manufacturer for viscosity correction.

the cutting of the magnetic lines by the conductive liquid. A pair of detection electrodes are
installed on the pipe wall perpendicular to the axis of the measuring pipe and the magnetic
lines to detect this induced voltage.

1.2.
Main Features and Applications
The electromagnetic flow meter consists of the sensor and the converter. The SFE910
electromagnetic flow meter measures the volume flow of various conductive liquids or
liquid-solid two-phase media, such as acids, alkalis, salt solutions, pulp, and mud. It is
widely used in chemical, metallurgical, water supply and drainage, sewage treatment, food,
sugar making, paper making, environmental protection and other industries.
The sensor has the following features:
（1）It adopts a welded integral structure with good sealing performance;
（2）The structure is simple and reliable, with no moving parts inside and almost no
pressure loss;
（3）It adopts low-frequency rectangular wave excitation, with good anti-interference
performance and stable zero point;
（4）The instrument measurement is not affected by changes in physical parameters such
as pressure, viscosity, temperature, and density of the measured medium;
（5）The instrument has a sensitive response, and the output signal is linearly related to
the flow, with a wide range ratio;
（6）Since the measured medium only contacts the lining of the measuring tube and the
electrode, it is easy to meet the requirements of corrosion resistance and wear
resistance;
（7）It has low power consumption; the power consumption of the whole instrument is
<10W, which is not related to the size of the sensor diameter;
（8）It is easy to install, use and maintain.

（6）Excitation System: Coils positioned at the top and bottom outside of the measuring

Pulse, Frequency Output
This converter's frequency and pulse outputs are galvanically isolated, and internal and

The converter's frequency and pulse outputs use a transistor output method. The maximum
pulse output frequency is 5 kHz, with an active output (internal power supply) mode having
an output amplitude of 15V; the load resistance must be ≥600Ω and <5kΩ. When using an
external power supply, the supply voltage must not exceed 30V, and the current in the loop
after connecting the load must not exceed 50mA to avoid damaging the instrument.

item “Pulse Equivalent P/L.”

The flow direction setting is used to adjust the direction on-site. "Forward" indicates that the
flow meter's forward direction is consistent with the on-site flow direction. If the flow
direction is opposite to the flow meter's forward direction, the flow direction should be set to
"Reverse," which will reverse the flow meter's forward direction.
Enabling bidirectional flow means that forward and reverse flows will be measured and
displayed. Turning off bidirectional flow means only forward flow will be measured and
displayed.
Changing the flow direction redefines the flow meter's forward direction, and the
accumulated values in each counter will also change. Modifying the flow direction does
not change the counter value. It is recommended that all counters be reset to zero after
changing the flow direction.

X600 Interactive Intelligent Calibrator & Handheld Communicator
The X600 series interactive Intelligent calibrator & handheld communicator is a handheld
tool that combines a Intelligent calibrator and HART communicator in one device. It features
a capacitive full-touch screen with a 1080P high-definition display. The device boasts a
unique detachable operation design, allowing the operation terminal to be separated for
independent use, providing convenience for on-site operations. The dual-channel full
isolation design supports dual independent output and measurement, with a signal
accuracy of up to 0.01%. The product offers easy-to-use modules like process calibration
and data recording, enabling electronic archival of calibration and recording operations.At
the same time, APL Ethernet on-site can be supported through expansion modules.
The device comes with over 1,000 built-in DD files (covering all HART Foundation certified
HART products) and can perform configuration, calibration, and troubleshooting for field
instruments like transmitters, positioners, and flow meters from various domestic and
international brands.

A valve positioner is an auxiliary control instrument used in industrial automation process
control. It is designed to improve the static and dynamic characteristics of control valves,
enhance control accuracy and speed, and increase control flexibility. The positioner, in
conjunction with the valve and actuator, forms a control valve and creates a closed-loop
control system through input and feedback signals. The valve positioner plays a critical role
as the core control component in a control valve.

4.2
Initialization
After installing the valve positioner on the actuator, initialization is necessary. There are two
methods for initialization: automatic calibration and manual calibration.
*Note:This section focuses on the operational steps for each menu; detailed explanations are
provided in Chapter 5.
4.2.1
Initialization preparation

Ensure that the positioner is correctly installed, connected to the air source,
wired ,and powered according to Chapter 2.

Ensure the positioner is correctly installed and the valve's stroke is set to the
midpoint (i.e., the stroke pointer is around 50% on the scale). If not, manually
adjust the position to the midpoint as described in Section 4.3. The feedback
rod should be approximately horizontal with the positioner body; adjust the
installation position if necessary.

After completing the above preparation, the display value should be within
(50±5)% in preset mode. If not, use one hand to adjust the sensor adjustment
lever (refer to Figure 2-3) to separate the large and small gears in the gear
group-18. With the other hand, adjust the small gear to set the display value
to (50±5)%.

To reinitialize, follow the instructions in Section 4.2.4—[Factory Reset]—to
clear operational data and enter preset mode.
4.2.2
Automatic calibration
This function automatically completes the stroke and control calibration with a single button
press. The positioner will sequentially measure the direction of action, stroke, and actuator
stroke time, and configure control parameters based on dynamic conditions of the actuator.
To initiate automatic calibration, long-press the
+
button on the main control
interface to enter the initialization menu. If the positioner has not been initialized before, it
will display the preset interface, and the above steps should be performed in this mode.


Before pressurizing, ensure that the process connections are installed and tightened.






protective measures should be taken against lightning strikes.

To prevent process media from spilling, do not loosen or remove process flange bolts,


When draining condensate from pressurized parts, avoid contact with skin, eyes, or other



hazardous locations.


equipment, its structure, installation, wiring, and maintenance must strictly meet safety
requirements, otherwise, it may cause danger.

When welding pipelines, prevent welding currents from passing through the transmitter.

Avoid contact with or inhalation of toxic or harmful accumulated liquids (or gases).

If the ambient temperature is below the freezing point of the measured medium, take
antifreeze measures to prevent the medium from freezing within the transmitter and impulse
lines, which could damage the sensor diaphragm and the transmitter.

If the loop is not designed for non-flammable environments, it is crucial to avoid igniting
flammable environments nearby. To prevent fire, use metal conduit.

All wiring should comply with local installation requirements and electrical codes.

It is recommended that users use metal conduit or shielded twisted-pair cables to connect
signal lines to meet EMC requirements.

After connecting, close the process pressure outlet valve (main valve), transmitter valve (cutoff

external impurities from entering the impulse line.

Do not rotate pressurized parts more than 180°.

When using a differential pressure transmitter to measure low pressure, the low-pressure side
should be open to the atmosphere. Wind near the atmospheric inlet may cause measurement
errors. To avoid this, install an appropriate restrictor valve on the low-pressure side, and place
the atmospheric inlet and transmitter inside a box.

Before shutting down, cut off the power; if shutting down for an extended period, close the
pressure valve and drain the fluid from the impulse line and sensing unit to prevent freezing or
corrosion.

Do not step on the instrument.

Instrument repair and parts replacement must be performed by SUPCON professionals.

Chapter1
Overview
1.1 Overview
The CXT-SKC Multi-Variable Flow Transmitter is designed to measure differential pressure,
pressure, and temperature signals of various fluids. For steam and general gas media, it can
further compensate and calculate the flow and cumulative values of the medium. All
measured data can be output via RS485 or HART signals.
The CXT-SKC transmitter is generally used in conjunction with a standard orifice device.
1.2 Operating Principle
The CXT-SKC transmitter is available in two versions based on communication type: HART
and APL versions.
See Figure 1-1 for the HART version schematic.
HART Version: This version operates on a 24V two-wire power supply and supports
(4-20)mA and HART output. When the input signal changes, the electrical signal of the
detection unit changes proportionally. After processing and amplifying by the conversion unit,
the corresponding RS485 or HART+(4-20)mA signal is output.
Figure 1-1 Block diagram of HART version
*Note: When RS485 is enabled on the HART version, the (4~20)mA output is fixed at 12mA, and
data is output through the RS485 bus.
See Figure 1-2 for the APL version schematic.
APL Version: This version operates with a two-wire APL bus power supply, and data is
transmitted via the bus. Some instrument parameters can be configured using the SUPCON
VxIDM software, with specific communication configuration referenced in the "VxIDM

1.3 Safety Precautions
To avoid unnecessary harm, it is essential to understand the hazards of handling the product
in hazardous locations. To prevent damage during transportation, keep the product in its
original packaging until it reaches the worksite. For long-term storage, consider the
following:

Protect from rain, impact, and vibration. Ensure that the air is free of substances
that could corrode the transmitter.

Maintain the original packaging condition.

If storing a used product, thoroughly clean the residual liquid from the high and
low-pressure sides of the flange. Ensure that the conversion and detection units
are securely fastened. Avoid contact with or inhalation of toxic or harmful residual
liquids (or gases).

Do not step on the instrument.
Explosions can result in severe injury or death. When installing the transmitter in explosive
environments, you must follow all relevant local, national, and international standards, codes,
and practices.

Do not remove the transmitter cover during operation in explosion-proof
installations.

Disconnect the circuit before opening the cover. Install according to the
instructions in the manual.

Ensure the operating environment meets the appropriate hazardous area
certification.

Before connecting a HART communicator in an explosive environment, ensure
that the loop devices have been installed according to intrinsic safety or
non-flammable location wiring rules.
Process leaks can result in severe injury or death.

After unpacking, please verify that the instrument matches the order specifications.
The transmitter can be installed either by piping or wall-mounting. For wall-mounting, please
provide M8 bolts. Level transmitters require flange mounting.
4.1.1
Selection of Installation Location
The CXT series intelligent pressure transmitter is designed with waterproof and dustproof
features, making it suitable for installation in various locations. However, to facilitate daily
maintenance, extend the instrument ’ s lifespan, and ensure reliability, an appropriate
installation location should be selected. The installation site should meet the following
conditions:
1)
Sufficient Working Space: Ensure adequate space around the instrument, with a
distance of more than 0.5 meters from adjacent objects in all directions, to facilitate
installation, piping, wiring, and routine maintenance.
2)
No Corrosive Gases: Avoid environments with corrosive gases. Use protective
covers or anti-corrosion paint if the environment is corrosive.

To prevent interference from vibrations of the transmitter and capillary tube, install

When measuring gas, ensure the pressure guide tube from the transmitter to the



inlet is inclined upwards with a slope of at least 1/10 to prevent liquid
accumulation in the detection unit.

Avoid sharp bends in the pressure guide tube to prevent gas or liquid
accumulation, which could affect measurement.

Avoid improper use of external forces.

The material of the pressure guide tube should meet the temperature and
pressure requirements of the measured medium.

Use heaters for insulation to prevent freezing of fluids in the detection unit.


All wiring must comply with the manual instructions and local electrical regulations.

Voltages exceeding 45VDC between the transmitter’s “+” and “-” terminals


Use shielded cables for transmission lines.

To avoid interference, signal wires must not be installed in the same conduit or
cable tray as power cables.

Wiring in explosion-proof areas must adhere to national regulations for such
environments.

Before wiring, ensure the main power is turned off to prevent electric shock.
Use the correct rated cables to prevent fire hazards.
After installing the transmitter, secure the transmitter unit cover and terminal box to prevent
rainwater from entering, which could cause transmitter failure or incorrect operation.
It is recommended to use metal conduits or shielded twisted pairs for signal connections to
meet EMC requirements.

For Explosion-Proof Products:
Use explosion-proof connectors specified by the manufacturer. Customers may also use
explosion-proof connectors that meet the explosion-proof certification requirements,
provided they have the necessary certification, and connect cables according to the
explosion-proof structure.

Chapter 1 Overview

Chapter 1
Overview
The CXT transmitter detects the differential pressure or pressure of various fluids, converts
it into a current signal of 4 to 20mA DC and transmits it.
All the adjustment functions are incorporated in the amplifier unit for making adjustments
easily and exactly.
Transmitter settings (such as range and damping time constant, etc.) can be changed from
an HHC (Hand Held Communicator) or a local configurator unit with LCD display.
1.1
Principle
The operating principle of the CXT smart transmitter is shown in the block diagram below.
The input pressure is changed into an electrostatic capacitance in the detecting unit. The
change proportional to the pressure undergoes conditioning and amplification in the
amplifier unit, and is then output as a current of 4 to 20mA DC.

Installation
After unpacking, check the delivered items.

The transmitter is heavy. Be careful when handling it.
a) The transmitter should be installed in a place that meets the operating conditions shown
in Data Sheet or Instruction Manual.

to the cause of fall, trouble or incorrect operation.
c) When installing, make sure that the transmitter interior is free from cable chips and other
foreign objects to prevent fire, trouble or incorrect operation.

store it in a room at the normal temperature and humidity (25℃, 60%RH).

Non-explosion-proof transmitter must not be used in a place with explosive
gas to prevent serious accidents such as explosion, fire, etc.

(5) Cautions on impulse piping

For liquid, the impulse pipes should have an upward slope of 1/10 or more between
the process connection and the transmitter to prevent accumulation of gas, etc.
in the detecting unit.

For gas, the impulse pipes should have a downward slope of 1/10 or more between
the process connection and transmitter to prevent accumulation of moisture,
etc. in the detecting unit.

Do not blow down impulse piping through the transmitter. For steam service, first,
isolate the transmitter then flush the lines and refill the lines with water before
resuming measurement.

Avoid any sharp bends in impulse pipe which may cause gas or moisture to
accumulate in the impulse pipe.

In order to prevent vibration of the transmitter body and capillary from interfering with
output, the transmitter body should be installed at a vibration-free place and
the capillary should be fixed to a stable support.

Take care not to apply an excessive force to the transmitter during its connection.

The impulse pipes used should be suitable for the working temperature, pressure, etc.

When the measuring fluid is likely to freeze in the cover of the measurement chamber,
the cover needs to be warmed up with steam or a heater.

After completing the connections, close the valves on the process pressure taps (main
valves), the valves at the transmitter (stop valves), and the impulse piping drain

Appendix 1 Built-in Arrester
65
Appendix 1 Built-in Arrester
An arrester is used to protect a transmitter or receiver from an abnormal voltage such as
lightning surges induced into signal lines. A built-in type arrester is mounted behind the
terminal unit. A nameplate marked “with arrester” is attached to the terminal unit of
transmitter with a built-in arrester.
Appendix 1.1
Installation
The built-in arrester should be used in combination with panel mounting type arrester for
distributor protection.
Appendix 1.2
Grounding
Since transmitter and arrester groundings are internally connected together, users have
only to connect the external grounding terminals to ground.
Grounding terminal must be used, in case of the explosion-proof or intrinsic safety type
transmitter.
Grounding resistance should be 100Ωor less.
Avoid common grounding with a lightning rod.
Appendix 1.3
Maintenance
Check of arrester:
(1) Measure output current from the transmitter check terminals and output current to flow
into transmitter. When current is measured with an ammeter connected to CHECK+ and

CXT Intelligent Pressure Transmitter
66
CHECK- terminals, the internal resistance of the ammeter should be 12Ωor less.
(2) If the measured two output current are the same, the arrester is normal.
(3) In case the measured values have a difference of 0.1% (0.016mA) or more, the arrester
is not functioning.
(4) In the above case, the arrester unit (terminal unit) should be replaced with a new one.

1.1 Summarize
The CXT transmitter detects the differential pressure or pressure of various fluids, converts
it into a current signal of 4 to 20mA DC and transmits it.
Transmitter settings (such as range and damping time constant, etc.) can be changed from
an HHC (Hand Held Communicator).
1.2 Principle Of Operation
The operating principle of the CXT smart transmitter is shown in the block diagram below.
The input pressure is changed into an electrostatic capacitance in the sensor. The change
proportional to the pressure undergoes conditioning and amplification in the amplifier unit,
and is then output as a current of 4 to 20mA DC.
Figure 1- 1
1.3 Safety Precautions
To avoid unnecessary injury, be sure to understand the hazards of handling products in
hazardous locations. To prevent damage during handling, keep the product in its factory
packaging until it reaches the work site. The following points should be noted when storing
the product for a long period of time:

Protect from rain, shock, and vibration, and the air should be free of hazardous
substances sufficient to cause corrosion of the transmitter.

Keep the product in the original packaging condition when it is shipped from the
factory.

Keep the used products, should thoroughly wash the residual liquid inside the high
and low pressure sides of the flange, and also make sure that the conversion unit
and detection unit have been tightened as required. Avoid contact with or inhalation
of toxic and hazardous fluids (or gases).

Do not step on the meter.
Explosions can cause significant injury or death. When the transmitter is installed in an
explosion-prone environment, the relevant local and national standards as well as
international standards, regulations and practices must be followed.

Chapter 4
Installation and Piping
4.1 Installation
After unpacking, check the delivered items.
This transmitter can be mounted on a pipe or on a wall. However, level transmitters require
flange mounting.
Note that the bolts (M8) for wall mounting should be supplied by the customer.
4.1.1 On site condition
The CXT smart pressure transmitter is waterproof and dust-proof and can be installed
anywhere. However, in order to facilitate daily maintenance operations, extend the service
life of the instrument and ensure reliability, the appropriate installation site should be
selected, and the installation site should meet the following conditions:
a) There is sufficient working space around, and the distance from adjacent objects
(in any direction) is greater than 0.5 meters, so as to facilitate installation, piping, wiring and
daily maintenance.
b) There is no corrosive gas around. For corrosive environments need to use
protective cover or anti-corrosion paint to prevent corrosion.
c) There is no strong induction interference around, and it is not easy to produce
static electricity, magnetic field or noise interference.
d) No direct sunlight.
e) Although the design is based on high-frequency noise resistance, the installation
position should be avoided with high-power frequency converter and high-frequency
electrical appliances installed together, and a certain distance should be left. The
transmitter connection cable should not be laid on the same bridge as the cable of
high-power equipment to ensure that the loop is not affected by noise.
f) Others shall meet the requirements of normal working conditions.

If the transmitter is not used soon after delivery, then leave it packed and
store it in a room at the normal temperature and humidity (25℃, 60%RH).

as shown in Figure 4-1.

(6) Cautions on impulse pipe


When the measuring fluid is likely to freeze in the cover of the measurement chamber,
the cover needs to be warmed up with steam or a heater.

5.1 Cautions on wiring

All wiring shall comply with manual requirements and local electrical regulations.

Application of a voltage exceeding 45 VDC or 32 VAC between “+” and “–” terminals
may result in damage to the transmitter.

Use a shielded cable for the transmission line where possible.

Avoid installation of signal cable and power cable in same conduit or cable tray in
order to prevent increased noise.

In case of an explosion proof arrangement, wiring shall be made in accordance with
the relevant regulations to ensure the explosion proofing.

Please use the communication equipment 20cm away from the transmitter and cable,
otherwise it may affect the output of the transmitter.

Electric shocks can cause serious injuries. Avoid touching wiring terminals. A high
voltage may be generated on terminals, which may cause an electric shock.

When using a power supply not having a non-incendive circuit, please pay attention
not to ignite in the surrounding flammable atmosphere. In such a case, we
recommend using wiring metal conduit in order to prevent the ignition.
5.2 Wiring procedure
Before making wiring work, be sure to turn OFF the main power to prevent electric shocks.
Use wiring materials of correct rating to prevent fire accidents.
After installing the transmitter, firmly close the covers of the amplifier unit and terminal box.
If not, rain water will enter the transmitter which may result in trouble or incorrect operation.
It is recommended that users use metal wire tube or shielded twisted-pair wire to connect
the signal line to meet the requirements of EMC.
(1) Sealing of conduit connection

Regular and intrinsically safe products
Use sealing tape, if using metal pipe screw coupling or rubber gasket and fastening gland
in the case of cable (outside diameter ø11) to ensure air tightness of the connection box.

Flameproof products
Need to choose our designated flameproof joint; Customers can also fit flameproof joints
that meet the requirements of flameproof (need to obtain a flameproof certificate), and
connect cables according to the flameproof structure.

6.1 Preparation for operation
Before operating the transmitter, be sure to perform the following checks and procedures.

On zero point check or zero adjustment in hazardous area, use the external
zero adjust screw. Do not open terminal cover and do not use HHC.
6.1.1 Preparation procedure
(1) Check for liquid or gas leakage from the pressure connector, etc. by applying soapy
water or the like.
(2) Check the signal wiring according to the “Terminal block connection diagram” shown in
5.2.
(3) Vent gas from the transmitter in the case of liquid measurement.
(4) Perform zero point adjustment.
Figure 6- 1 Preparation for operation

When the plant requires chemical cleaning at the start of operation, be sure
to close the valve of the transmitter to prevent entry of cleaning liquid into
the pressure sensor.
6.1.2 Zero adjustment
Turn on the power to the transmitter.
Check the output signal of the transmitter by connecting a DC ammeter across CHECK+
and CHECK- of the terminal unit.
After ten minutes or longer, adjust the transmitter output current to 4 mA (zero adjustment).

Adjustment by zero zero adjust screw
Adjust zero point of the transmitter to 4 mA by turning the zero zero adjust screw.

Introduction of functional blocks
The FF pressure transmitter conforms to the foundation fieldbus standard. The user layer
consists of a resource block, a transducer block, and a functional block with 1 resource
blocks, 2 transducer blocks, and 3 AI functional blocks. The FF pressure transmitter is
operated by the VFFFBuilder tool in VisualField software. The specific VFFFBuilder
configuration is referred to the FF configuration software manual. The FF pressure
transmitter block is shown in Figure 8-4 as shown in VFFFBuilder software.

transmitter is shown in Table 8-1.

number. The resource block has no input or output parameters. The FF

conversion card is used to collect data from the pressure value and its own

The analog input function block is used to obtain the input data of the

Figure 10-6 Vibration Measurement Scenarios for Mixing Tanks
In the vibration measurement scenario depicted in Figure 10-6, the medium in the

routine monitoring. This vibration measurement transmitter effectively meets such
usage requirements. Furthermore, to ensure more precise vibration measurement,
the transmitter should be installed close to the motor's installation position (such as

11.1 Periodic inspection
In order to ensure the measurement accuracy and long life of the transmitter, it is essential
to inspect the transmitter periodically according to the operating conditions.
(1) Visual inspection
Visually inspect each part of the transmitter for damage, corrosion, etc. If you detect any
material which may cause corrosion, it should be cleaned off.
(2) Check of cover and O-ring
The transmitter has a water and dust-proof construction. Make sure the O-ring of the case
cover is not damaged or deteriorated. Carefully prevent process outside materials from
sticking to threads.

(3) Piping leakage check
Using soapy water or the like, check the all pressure connectors for leakage of process
fluid. If necessary, drain the moisture which has accumulated in the transmitter and impulse
pipe.

An arrester is used to protect a transmitter or receiver from an abnormal voltage such as
lightning surges induced into signal lines. A built-in type arrester is mounted behind the
terminal unit. A nameplate marked “with arrester” is attached to the terminal unit of
transmitter with a built-in arrester.

Installation
The built-in arrester should be used in combination with panel mounting type arrester for
distributor protection.
Appendix 3.2
Grounding
Since transmitter and arrester groundings are internally connected together, users have
only to connect the external grounding terminals to ground.
Grounding terminal must be used, in case of the flameproof or intrinsic safety type
transmitter.
Grounding resistance should be 100Ωor less.
Avoid connecting with the grounding of the lightning protection module.

Chapter1 Product Overview
1
Chapter1
Product Overview
1.1 Product Summary
The vortex flowmeter is a device based on the Kármán vortex street principle, used to measure the
flow of liquids, gases, and steam. It can also measure turbid liquids containing small particles and
impurities. This flowmeter is widely used in industries such as petroleum, chemicals, pharmaceuticals,
paper manufacturing, metallurgy, power generation, environmental protection, and food processing.
1.2 Working Principle
The LUGB type vortex flowmeter operates based on the theories related to vortex generation and the
relationship between vortex frequency and flow rate as established by Kármán and Strouhal. As
shown in Figure 1, a triangular column, known as the vortex generator, is inserted vertically within the
flowmeter body. When the medium flows through the body, alternating and regular Kármán vortices
are generated behind the triangular column. The vortex shedding frequency F is proportional to the
flow velocity V of the medium. By detecting the number of vortices using a sensor, the fluid flow rate
can be calculated, and subsequently, the volumetric flow rate of the medium can be determined based
on the diameter of the flowmeter body.
The formulae are as follows:
F=St×V/md
Equation 1
Q=3600×F/K
Equation 2
M=Q×ρ
Equation 3
Where:
F
Vortex frequency generated by the fluid passing through the triangular column of the vortex
flowmeter (Unit: Hz)
St
Strouhal number (dimensionless)
V
Average fluid velocity in the pipeline (Unit: m/s)
m
Ratio of the bow-shaped flow area on both sides of the triangular column to the cross-sectional
area of the measuring pipe (dimensionless)
d
Width of the upstream face of the triangular column within the vortex flowmeter body (Unit: m)
D
Inner diameter of the vortex flowmeter body (Unit: m)
Q
Instantaneous volumetric flow rate (Unit: m³/h)
K
Flowmeter coefficient (Unit: pulses per cubic meter)
M
Instantaneous mass flow rate (Unit: kg/h)
ρ
Fluid density (unit: kg/ m3)
Note: The flowmeter coefficient K varies for different diameters of vortex flowmeters. The specific value is
obtained through actual calibration of the flowmeter using a flow calibration device, representing the number of
pulses output by the sensor per cubic meter of fluid under working conditions.

Chapter3
Installation and Wiring
3.1 Selection of Installation Location and Environment
1)
Avoid strong electrical equipment, high-frequency variable frequency equipment, and high-power
switching equipment as much as possible.
2)
Avoid high-temperature heat sources and radiative heat sources as much as possible; for outdoor
installations, ensure proper sunshade and rainproof measures.
3)
Avoid areas with strong vibrations and highly corrosive environments as much as possible; also
consider ease of installation and maintenance.
3.2 Selection of Installation Position
1)
The installation position should avoid strongly vibrating pipelines; otherwise, vibration reduction
measures, such as adding vibration dampers, must be taken.
2)
The flowmeter can be installed horizontally, vertically, or at an incline. When measuring liquids,
ensure the fluid flows from a lower to a higher position; when measuring gases, the flow direction
is not limited; when measuring steam or high-temperature gases, the meter body should
preferably be installed at a 45° angle to the vertical direction.
3.3 Grounding Requirements
When installing the flowmeter, the meter body should be reliably grounded. If the onsite pipeline does
not have grounding conditions, a separate ground wire should be connected to the grounding terminal
of the instrument housing.
3.4 Straight Pipe Section Requirements
For accurate measurement, sufficient straight pipe sections must be left upstream and downstream of
the flowmeter. The upstream section should not have any components that affect fluid velocity
distribution. The following diagrams show the straight pipe section requirements for various pipeline
configurations. The dimensions for the LUGB vortex flowmeter's straight pipe sections are shown in
the diagrams below.

The pipeline should be insulated to prevent the amplifier from being damaged by excessive ambient

4.1 X3-2 Amplifier
4.1.1 Functional Features
Function
Description
Auto Recovery
The amplifier has a factory parameter backup function. In case of parameter
confusion, users can restore factory settings through the menu, ensuring normal
instrument measurement.
Temperature and
pressure compensation
The amplifier software is equipped with measurement compensation modes suitable
for various media. Temperature and pressure can be automatically acquired or set
manually.
Output Types
The amplifier offers multiple output options, including "Working Condition Frequency
Output," "Equivalent Pulse Output," two-wire "(4 to 20)mA Current," and two-wire
"Current Percentage." The upper limit of current output can be set arbitrarily in the
menu via buttons without recalibrating zero and full scale.
Linear Correction
The amplifier software provides a 10-point linear instrument coefficient difference
algorithm. Based on actual calibration, up to 10-point linear correction settings can be
made to improve flowmeter measurement accuracy.
Output Protection
The amplifier includes overvoltage and overcurrent protection circuits. When choosing
the (4 to 20)mA current output, if the current value corresponding to the flow exceeds
22.8mA, the system will stabilize the current at 22.8mA to prevent excessive current.
Input Protection
It includes overvoltage and overcurrent protection at the input to prevent damage to
the amplifier from voltage or current spikes.
Auto Zero Adjustment
The amplifier has an automatic zero adjustment feature. When the pipeline flow is
zero, a light press of the button for 8 to 10 seconds will complete the instrument zero
setting.
Power Interruption Query
It can query the last 10 power interruption times (optional).
The amplifier automatically switches between battery and external power.

1.1 Product Overview
The SF20 Series Intelligent Metal Tube Variable Area Flowmeter is a widely used flow
measuring instrument in industrial automation process control. It features a compact design,
broad detection range, and ease of use, making it suitable for measuring the flow of liquids,
gases, and steam. It is particularly effective for low flow rates, small flow volumes, high
temperatures, high pressures, strong corrosive conditions, and both conductive and non-
conductive media.
This series of metal tube flowmeters adheres to the Q/ZKYB102.00024-2020 enterprise
standard and meets the JB/T 6844-2015 national standard. The product is calibrated in
accordance with JJG257-2007 calibration regulations.
It has been inspected and certified by a national quality inspection agency for explosion
protection,
complying
with
GB3836.1-2010,
GB3836.2-2010,
and
GB3836.4-2010
standards. Its explosion-proof markings are: Exd II C T1T6 Gb for flameproof and Exia IIC
T1T6 Gb for intrinsic safety.
1.2 Working Principle
When the measured medium flows from the bottom to the top through the measuring tube,
a differential pressure is created at the top and bottom of the float, generating an upward
force. When this upward force exceeds the weight of the float immersed in the fluid, the
float rises. As the float rises, the annular gap area increases, causing a rapid decrease in
the fluid velocity at the annular gap. This results in a reduction in the differential pressure
across the float, which decreases the upward force until it balances with the weight of the
float. At this point, the float stabilizes at a certain position, with the float position
corresponding to the flow rate of the measured medium.
The float contains a built-in magnet. As the float moves up and down with the medium, the
magnetic field changes. The indicator, which has a follow-up magnet fixed on the pointer
shaft, couples with the magnet in the float, driving the pointer and the sensing magnet to
rotate. The pointer indicates the local instantaneous flow rate on the scale plate. This is
converted into an electrical signal by a magnetic sensor, processed by the circuitry, and
displayed as both instantaneous flow rate and cumulative flow rate.

Chapter5 Installation and Usage Precautions
5.1 General Requirements
The general requirements for the installation and use of the instrument are as follows:
(1)
Handling and Transportation: The instrument is a precision device and must be
handled with care during transport, installation, storage, and use. Avoid rough handling,
overstressing during installation, and improper storage. Ensure the relative position of the
indicator and sensor remains unchanged, as any shift can directly affect measurement
accuracy.
(2)
Pipe Cleaning Before Installation: Before installing the instrument, clean the
process pipeline to prevent ferromagnetic substances from adhering inside the instrument,
which can degrade its performance or even cause damage. If such substances cannot be
avoided, install a magnetic filter at the instrument's inlet. Do not include the instrument in
the pipeline's pre-operational gas blowout to prevent damage.
(3)
Preparation
Before
Installation:
Remove
the
packing
material
inside
the
measuring tube that restrains the float (to prevent movement during transport) and inspect
the instrument for any damage sustained during transport.
(4)
Vertical Installation: Ensure the instrument's centerline deviates less than 2 °
from the plumb line.Horizontal Installation: For SF20 models, ensure the instrument ’ s
horizontal centerline deviates less than 2° from the level line, and the centerline of vertical
pipes should also deviate less than 2° from the plumb line.
(5)
Piping Connections: The upstream and downstream pipes should match the
instrument’s nominal diameter, and the flanges or threads should be compatible with the
instrument. The upstream straight pipe length should be 5 times the instrument's nominal
diameter, with a downstream straight pipe length of at least 250mm.
(6)
Avoiding Magnetic Interference: Since the instrument transmits signals through
magnetic coupling, to ensure accuracy, avoid placing ferromagnetic materials within a 10cm
radius of the instrument. For dense, side-by-side installations, maintain a spacing of at least
300mm.
(7)
Pressure and Flow Stability for Gas Measurement: Instruments calibrated at
0.1MPa and 20℃with air may experience pressure drops at the float if gas is discharged
directly into the atmosphere, causing pointer fluctuations. Install a valve at the instrument's
outlet and adjust it to reduce the valve opening during operation.
(8)
Stress-Free Installation: The instrument should not be subjected to stress when

Chapter5 Installation and Usage Precautions
17
installed in the pipeline. Ensure proper pipe supports at the inlet and outlet to minimize
stress on the instrument.
(9)
PTFE-Lined Instruments: When installing instruments with PTFE linings, be
cautious of potential deformation under pressure. Use the provided PTFE gaskets to
prevent the liner from cracking due to over-compression.
(10) Regular Cleaning: Over time, ferromagnetic substances in the pipeline may
adhere to the float, potentially jamming it or affecting measurement accuracy. Periodically
clean the measuring tube. If a magnetic filter is installed, clean it regularly as well.
(11) Protection Against Environmental Contaminants: The instrument's indicator
contains electronic components, so when disassembling or using the instrument, tighten the
screws or cover to maintain the seal. Prevent liquids and ferromagnetic substances from
entering the instrument and ensure the housing is reliably grounded.
(12) First-Time Use Precautions:

Liquid Measurement: Open the valve slowly to avoid water hammer that could
damage the instrument.

Gas Measurement: Do not pressurize the pipeline before opening the valve.
Rapid opening can cause the float to surge against the stopper, potentially
damaging the instrument. Consider using a pneumatic damping device to
minimize float oscillations.
(13) Smart Indicator Setup: Ensure correct electrical wiring before powering up the
instrument to avoid damage. Operate the instrument's buttons according to the user manual
to prevent data loss or corruption in the EEPROM.
(14) Storage Conditions: Store the instrument in environments with temperatures
between -40℃to 55℃, relative humidity not exceeding 90%, and no exposure to rain, snow,
sunlight, or corrosive gases.
(15) Avoid Water Damage: During cleaning, do not rinse the instrument housing with
water to prevent water ingress and potential damage.
(16) Pressure Considerations: Ensure that the medium pressure at the installation site
exceeds the flowmeter's pressure loss.
(17) LCD Display Protection: Avoid direct sunlight on the LCD to extend its lifespan.
(18) Low-Temperature Measurements: If no insulation or vacuum jacket was ordered,
insulate the instrument onsite when measuring low-temperature media.
(19) Electrical Connections: Verify the instrument's power supply and output mode
before wiring. Confirm the correct terminal numbers on the circuit board for power and
signal connections to avoid damage.
(20) Compliance with Manual: Follow this manual's guidelines to ensure correct and
safe use of the instrument.

1.2.
Main Features and Applications
The electromagnetic flow meter consists of the sensor and the converter. The SFE900
electromagnetic flow meter measures the volume flow of various conductive liquids or
liquid-solid two-phase media, such as acids, alkalis, salt solutions, pulp, and mud. It is
widely used in chemical, metallurgical, water supply and drainage, sewage treatment, food,
sugar making, paper making, environmental protection and other industries.
The sensor has the following features:
（1）It adopts a welded integral structure with good sealing performance;
（2）The structure is simple and reliable, with no moving parts inside and almost no
pressure loss;
（3）It adopts low-frequency rectangular wave excitation, with good anti-interference
performance and stable zero point;
（4）The instrument measurement is not affected by changes in physical parameters such
as pressure, viscosity, temperature, and density of the measured medium;
（5）The instrument has a sensitive response, and the output signal is linearly related to
the flow, with a wide range ratio;
（6）Since the measured medium only contacts the lining of the measuring tube and the
electrode, it is easy to meet the requirements of corrosion resistance and wear
resistance;
（7）It has low power consumption; the power consumption of the whole instrument is
<10W, which is not related to the size of the sensor diameter;

Menu Path: "Calibration" →"Empty Pipe Calibration".
Before the empty pipe calibration, ensure the flowmeter is installed and connected correctly
and that the grounding is accurate and reliable. Also, confirm that there is no medium in the
measuring tube of the flowmeter sensor.
Before performing the empty pipe calibration, the "Empty Pipe Switch" must be turned on.
To ensure accurate empty pipe detection, both "Empty Pipe Calibration" and "Full Pipe
Calibration" must be performed separately. Empty Pipe Calibration: Conducted when the
pipeline is in an empty pipe state. Full Pipe Calibration: Conducted when the pipeline is
filled with the medium. The process for both calibrations is the same. Using empty pipe
calibration as an example, the flowmeter enters the empty pipe calibration interface as

accuracy. Automatic calibration is recommended, and manual adjustments to calibration
results are generally unnecessary.
The entire pipe calibration process is similar to empty pipe calibration.

2.5.6.
Flow Direction
Flow Direction Menu Path: "Configuration" →"Flow Configuration" →"Flow Direction";
Bidirectional Flow Menu Path: "Configuration" →"Flow Configuration" →"Bidirectional
Flow".
The flow direction setting is used to adjust the direction on-site. "Forward" indicates that the
flow meter's forward direction is consistent with the on-site flow direction. If the flow
direction is opposite to the flow meter's forward direction, the flow direction should be set to
"Reverse," which will reverse the flow meter's forward direction.
Enabling bidirectional flow means that forward and reverse flows will be measured and
displayed. Turning off bidirectional flow means only forward flow will be measured and
displayed.
Changing the flow direction redefines the flow meter's forward direction, and the
accumulated values in each counter will also change. Modifying the flow direction
does not change the counter value. It is recommended that all counters be reset to
zero after changing the flow direction.

the cutting of the magnetic lines by the conductive liquid. A pair of detection electrodes are
installed on the pipe wall perpendicular to the axis of the measuring pipe and the magnetic
lines to detect this induced voltage.

1.2.
Main Features and Applications
The electromagnetic flow meter consists of the sensor and the converter. The SFE910
electromagnetic flow meter measures the volume flow of various conductive liquids or
liquid-solid two-phase media, such as acids, alkalis, salt solutions, pulp, and mud. It is
widely used in chemical, metallurgical, water supply and drainage, sewage treatment, food,
sugar making, paper making, environmental protection and other industries.
The sensor has the following features:
（1）It adopts a welded integral structure with good sealing performance;
（2）The structure is simple and reliable, with no moving parts inside and almost no
pressure loss;
（3）It adopts low-frequency rectangular wave excitation, with good anti-interference
performance and stable zero point;
（4）The instrument measurement is not affected by changes in physical parameters such
as pressure, viscosity, temperature, and density of the measured medium;
（5）The instrument has a sensitive response, and the output signal is linearly related to
the flow, with a wide range ratio;
（6）Since the measured medium only contacts the lining of the measuring tube and the
electrode, it is easy to meet the requirements of corrosion resistance and wear
resistance;
（7）It has low power consumption; the power consumption of the whole instrument is
<10W, which is not related to the size of the sensor diameter;
（8）It is easy to install, use and maintain.

The sensor structure is shown in Figure 2, the following components:
（1）Measuring tube: Measuring tube flow measured medium, measuring tube by the non-
magnetic stainless steel and welded flange, lined with insulation lining;
（2）Flange: Connection to the measuring pipe;
（3）Insulation Lining: the inside of the measuring tube and the flange sealing surface of a
complete corrosion-resistant electrical insulation material to prevent the traffic signal
from short-circuit;
（4）Electrode: with the magnetic field lines perpendicular to the direction of the
measurement pipe wall with a pair of electrodes to detect flow signals, the electrode
materials can be corrosion testing medium selected;
（5）Measurement Tube: The measured medium flows through the measurement tube,
which is made of non-magnetic stainless steel welded with flanges and lined with an
insulating liner;
（6）Excitation System: Coils positioned at the top and bottom outside of the measuring
tube create the operational magnetic field;
（7）Shell: The shell safeguards the instrument and ensures it is properly sealed.

The converter's frequency and pulse outputs use a transistor output method. The maximum
pulse output frequency is 5 kHz, with an active output (internal power supply) mode having
an output amplitude of 15V; the load resistance must be ≥600Ω and <5kΩ. When using an
external power supply, the supply voltage must not exceed 30V, and the current in the loop
after connecting the load must not exceed 50mA to avoid damaging the instrument.
Since the frequency and pulse output terminals are shared, selecting both output methods
is impossible. Users can choose the operating mode by setting the parameter item
“Configuration” →“Pulse Frequency” →“Digital Output Mode.”
The upper limit of the frequency output corresponding to the measured flow rate is
determined by the parameter item “Scaled Flow” (refer to the measurement range value on
the instrument's nameplate). The pulse output equivalent is determined by the parameter
item “Pulse Equivalent P/L.”

2.5.6.
Flow Direction
Flow Direction Menu Path: "Configuration" →"Flow Configuration" →"Flow Direction";
Bidirectional Flow Menu Path: "Configuration" →"Flow Configuration" →"Bidirectional
Flow".
The flow direction setting is used to adjust the direction on-site. "Forward" indicates that the
flow meter's forward direction is consistent with the on-site flow direction. If the flow
direction is opposite to the flow meter's forward direction, the flow direction should be set to
"Reverse," which will reverse the flow meter's forward direction.
Enabling bidirectional flow means that forward and reverse flows will be measured and
displayed. Turning off bidirectional flow means only forward flow will be measured and
displayed.
Changing the flow direction redefines the flow meter's forward direction, and the
accumulated values in each counter will also change. Modifying the flow direction does
not change the counter value. It is recommended that all counters be reset to zero after
changing the flow direction.

Chapter1 Product
1.1 SFM Series Coriolis Mass Flow Meters
The SFM series Coriolis mass flow meter is a high-precision flow measurement instrument
designed and manufactured based on the Coriolis force principle and mechanical vibration
characteristics. It can directly measure fluid's mass flow, density, and temperature
parameters. It applies to various industries such as petroleum, petrochemical, chemical,
paper-making, and new energy. It excels in process control and trade settlement, providing
accurate and reliable flow measurement solutions for industrial applications.
1.2 Product Composition
Figure 1 The SFM Series Coriolis Mass Flow Meter Consists of a Sensor and a Transmitter.
Sensor
This includes measuring tubes, vibration drivers (drive coils), signal detectors (sensing
coils), and temperature detection elements.
Transmitter
The microprocessor provides a driving force and completes the signal processing of the
primary device. It can calculate critical information such as mass flow by processing these
signals. Additionally, it provides the power supply and communication interfaces for the
mass flow meter.
1.3 Working Principle
The working principle of the Coriolis mass flow meter is based on the proportional
relationship between the Coriolis force generated by fluid flowing in a vibrating tube and the
mass flow rate.
The measuring tube inside the mass flow meter sensor vibrates under the action of a
driving force, generating parallel sinusoidal signals. When fluid flows through the sensor,

SFM800 Mass Flow Meter
2
the measuring tube deforms under the influence of the Coriolis force, causing a phase
difference at both ends of the measuring tube. The more significant the mass flow rate, the
more critical the phase difference. The mass flow meter transmitter can directly calculate
the fluid mass flow rate passing through the sensor by detecting and resolving this time
difference.
Figure 2 Working Principle Diagram
The measuring tube inside the sensor continuously vibrates at its resonant frequency.
Changes in the fluid density cause the resonant frequency of the measuring tube to change.
The mass flow meter transmitter detects and calculates the vibration frequency of the
measuring tube to determine the fluid density.
The mass flow meter sensor includes a precise temperature measurement component that
can measure and monitor the temperature of the measuring tube in real time. This
temperature can also be used for temperature compensation in mass flow and density
measurements.
1.4 Product Features
The Coriolis mass flow meter can directly measure the mass flow rate of the fluid in the
pipeline without the need for intermediate parameter conversion. It has high accuracy and
good repeatability, allowing for high-accuracy direct measurement of fluid mass flow over a
wide range.
The Coriolis mass flow meter can measure a wide range of fluids, including uniform fluids
with general viscosity, high-viscosity and non-Newtonian fluids, and even two-phase flows.
The measuring tube of the Coriolis mass flow meter has a slight vibration amplitude and
can be considered a non-moving part. There are no moving parts inside the flow meter
pipeline where the fluid flows, resulting in high reliability, long service life, and low daily
maintenance.
In addition to directly measuring the mass flow rate of the fluid, the Coriolis mass flow meter
can also directly measure the fluid density and temperature. It can calculate the
concentration of the solute in a two-component solution from the mass flow rate and fluid
density, making it a multifunctional flow measurement instrument.

Chapter4 Installation
4.1 Security Precautions
1. Ensure consideration of stress and loads due to earthquakes, transportation, and fires
during installation.
2. Ensure that the flow meter does not become a focal point for pipeline stress after
installation, as external loads are not considered in the flow meter design.
3. Provide adequate protection to minimise the risk of contact with hot surfaces.
4.2 Preparation Before Installation
1. Ensure the hazardous area classification specified on the mass flow meter label suits the
current installation environment.
2. Check the current ambient and process temperatures to ensure they are within the
instrument's specified limits.
3. The mass flow meter is suitable for indoor or outdoor installation, ensuring the pressure
does not exceed the rating indicated on the nameplate.
4.3 Installation Orientation
The flow direction indicator on the mass flow meter sensor housing should align with the
flow direction of the measured medium.
4.4 Installation Form
Select the most suitable installation form based on the measured medium and application
conditions.

4.5 Installation Guidelines
1. Minimize torque and bending loads on the process connections during the mass flow

SFM800 Mass Flow Meter
8
meter installation. Do not use the sensor to support the pipeline.
2. The mass flow meter should be firmly installed and secured on a support frame. Ensure
the installation area has no significant vibration sources. The operating temperature of the
electronic components should be within the range of -40℃to +55℃, with appropriate rain
and water protection measures.
3. Refer to the outline dimensions for installation dimensions.
4. Pay attention to the installation orientation and form.
5. Ensure the sensor is filled with the measured fluid to prevent gas accumulation inside
the sensor.
6. Install control valves downstream of the sensor.
7. Align the sensor coaxially with the pipeline, both axially and radially, aiming for zero-
stress installation.
8. In environments with solid vibrations, use expansion joints to eliminate the impact of
vibrations on the sensor.
9. When measuring vaporised media such as liquefied petroleum gas, propylene, and
propane quickly, ensure that the static pressure in the pipeline is greater than the medium's
saturated vapour pressure.
10. The mass flow meter requires zero-point calibration and periodic verification. Install
shut-off valves, a bypass, and shut-off valves upstream and downstream of the sensor.
11. The sensor installation position and method should avoid water hammer phenomena
for applications with intermittent feeding. Repeated start-stop operations should consider
process differentials. The sensor outlet should have a specific back pressure, and the
internal vibrating tube should be filled with liquid when feeding stops. If there is backflow or
the liquid cannot fill the tube, targeted solutions should be implemented to avoid affecting
measurement accuracy.

Chapter1 Product Introduction

Chapter1 Product Introduction
1.1 Product Overview
The Magnetic Float Level Gauge uses a float as the measurement element and a magnetic
steel to drive the magnetic indicator, requiring no external power. It features clear indication,
durability, no blind spots in measurement, and a wide measurement range. Since the
measurement display part does not come into direct contact with the medium, it is suitable
for high temperatures, high pressures, toxic, harmful, and strongly corrosive environments.
It
is
widely
used
in
industries
such
as
power,
petroleum,
chemical,
metallurgy,
environmental protection, shipping, construction, and food processing for liquid level
measurement and control.
1.2 Working Principle
The Magnetic Float Level Gauge operates based on the principle of buoyancy (Archimedes'
Principle) combined with magnetic coupling. As the liquid level in the container rises or falls,
the float inside the main tube of the gauge also rises or falls. The permanent magnet inside
the float transmits a magnetic signal through magnetic coupling to the on-site indicator
(scale), driving the magnetic indicators (columns or plates) to rotate. When the liquid level
rises, the columns (plates) change from black to yellow; when the liquid level falls, the
columns (plates) change from yellow to black. The boundary between yellow and black on
the indicator represents the actual liquid level height inside the container.
Magnetic Float and Indicator Panel Schematic Diagram


imple Structure: The level gauge has a straightforward structure, making it easy to
observe and maintain with minimal maintenance requirements.

connection methods, unaffected by the height of the storage tank.

with high reliability.

Complete Detection Function: It can measure both liquid levels and interfaces. In
addition to on-site indication, it can be equipped with remote transmitters and level
switches.

3.1 Installation

Model-Specific Installation: Refer to the schematic diagrams for installing different
models of the level gauge. For side-mounted installations, ensure that valves are
installed at both the upper and lower flanges of the level gauge for maintenance and
adjustment purposes.

Pre-Installation Calibration: Before installation, use a calibration magnet to turn the
magnetic columns (plates) on the level gauge to a black position.

Valve Operation: After installation, close the connection valves. Do not open the
valves before starting production or before flushing the pipeline, to prevent rust and
debris from the equipment from being attracted by the magnetic float.

Avoid Magnetic Interference: The main tube of the level gauge should not be exposed
to magnetic materials as the float is magnetic. Contact with such materials can affect
the normal measurement of the liquid level.

Startup Procedure: When putting into use, first open the upper valve, then slowly
open the lower valve to one-third of its capacity. After the liquid level stabilizes, open
the valve fully while observing whether the columns (plates) change from black to
yellow. If there is any flickering (yellow and black columns/plates crossing), calibrate
with the provided calibration magnet. Then close the lower valve, open the drainage
valve to observe if the level decreases, close the drainage valve, and reopen the
lower valve to check the liquid level.

Maintenance: Regularly clean the main tube and float based on the medium to
remove impurities and ensure proper operation.

4.1 Calibration Method for Non-Displaying Transmitters
The transmitters are rigorously calibrated before leaving the factory and generally do not
require recalibration before use. However, if recalibration is necessary for any reason,
follow these steps:
1
Move the magnetic float to the lower limit position (i.e., the zero position). The
current meter should read 4mA. If the deviation from 4mA exceeds the accuracy range,
adjust the zero potentiometer (ZERO) in the junction box.
2
lowly move the float along the guide rod to the full scale of the measurement range,
starting from the zero position. The current meter should read 20mA. If the deviation from
20mA exceeds the accuracy range, adjust the span potentiometer (FULL) in the junction
box.
3
After adjusting the zero and full scale, slowly move the float to the midpoint of the
range. The current meter should read 12mA.
4
Repeat the above steps two to three times to complete the calibration of the
transmitter.

Chapter6 Calibration Magnet's Usage
The calibration magnet is a standard accessory included with the product. It is used for the
following purposes:
Calibration of Indicator Pillar (Plate)
Handling Flipping Phenomenon:
When the indicator pillar or plate inside the level gauge's panel shows flipping (alternating
yellow and black indicators),hold the calibration magnet and place it near the protective
glass of the indicator pillar (plate);
Move the calibration magnet up and down, causing the indicator pillar (plate) to rotate with
the magnet;
Continue until the part of the indicator showing the level turns yellow and the part without
the level turns black. This will address the flipping phenomenon.
Identifying the True Level
When in doubt about the level indicated by the gauge:
Hold the calibration magnet and place it tightly against the outer wall of the level gauge's
main tube;
Move the calibration magnet up and down;
During the movement, you should feel a strong magnetic attraction where the magnetic
float is located, indicating the true level.
Note1: For accurate level identification, ensure that the magnetic float inside the main tube is in
normal condition (i.e., no blockages, no damage, and able to move up and down freely).
Note2: If there is a discrepancy between the indicated level and the true position, use the flipping
correction method to make adjustments.

Chapter1 Product Overview
